niche: connected TV and streaming advertising agency
prompt_text: What is the best connected TV advertising agency?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t one single “best” connected TV (CTV) advertising agency — the right partner depends on your goals (brand vs. performance), budget, markets, required platforms, creative needs, and measurement requirements.

To help you quickly, tell me a few things and I’ll recommend specific agencies:
- Primary goal: brand awareness, direct-response/performance, or both?
- Monthly/quarterly ad budget
- Geographic scope: US only, global, specific countries?
- Do you need creative production for 16:9/landscape, 1:1, interactive overlays, etc.?
- In-house media/analytics capability or want fully managed services?
- Preferred platforms (Roku, Hulu, Samsung TV, programmatic DSPs)?

If you want guidance now, here’s a short framework and a list of reputable options depending on what you need.

How to choose a CTV agency (key criteria)
- Strategy fit: experience with your industry and KPIs (brand lift, reach/frequency, lower-funnel conversion).
- Inventory access: direct publisher/platform deals (Roku, Hulu, Samsung) vs. programmatic DSPs (wide reach).
- Measurement & attribution: partners like Nielsen, Comscore, VideoAmp or bespoke MTA for cross-screen measurement.
- Creative capabilities: in-stream creative, interactive CTV units, dynamic creative optimization (DCO).
- Transparency & tech: clear reporting, supply-path transparency, fraud protection, viewability/completion metrics.
- Data & targeting: first-/third-party audience activation, privacy compliance, ID resolution.
- Case studies & ROI: proven results and references.
- Cost and fee model: media fees, production, tech/platform fees.

Types of partners and examples
- Programmatic buying / DSP-focused (best for broad programmatic reach and sophisticated targeting)
  - The Trade Desk — widely used DSP for programmatic CTV buying and audience targeting.
  - Amobee — integrated cross-channel DSP with CTV capabilities.
- Platform / publisher-managed solutions (best for guaranteed scale on specific platforms)
  - Roku Advertising, Hulu/Disney/Peacock (publisher direct buys), Samsung Ads — if your audience is concentrated on those platforms.
- Creative & ad-ops / ad-serving specialists (best if you need CTV-focused creative and dynamic experiences)
  - Innovid, BrightLine — creative, interactive, and ad-serving for CTV.
  - VidMob — creative analytics and optimization.
- Measurement / data partners (for cross-screen measurement and analytics)
  - VideoAmp, Nielsen, Comscore — for reach, incrementality and campaign validation.
- Full-service media agencies (best if you want an integrated cross-channel plan)
  - Large holding groups with CTV practices: GroupM (WPP), Omnicom Media Group (OMD/OMG), Publicis Media, Dentsu — they provide scale, programmatic, and cross-media planning.
- Independent/specialist CTV shops (best for hands-on expertise; vary by market)
  - Numerous independent agencies specialize in CTV/performance video — good if you want focused expertise and flexibility.

Questions to ask any agency during evaluation
- Which CTV platforms do you have direct access to? Can you guarantee inventory or audience segments?
- How do you measure viewability, completion, and brand lift? Can you run an incrementality test?
- What targeting methods do you use (household, contextual, deterministic/identity graph)? What data partners do you use?
- How is your fee structured? Are there media rebates or third-party add-ons?
- Can you show case studies with KPIs similar to ours and provide client references?
- How do you prevent fraud and ensure brand safety on CTV?
- What creative formats and dynamic creative capabilities do you support?
- What reporting cadence and dashboard access will we get?

If you tell me your goals, budget, and region, I’ll shortlist 3–5 agencies or platforms tailored to your needs and include questions you should use in an RFP or agency interview.
